question:
Text 1

In separate studies, Marine Fernandez and colleagues and Hualiang Zhang and colleagues examined whether plants transfer nutrients to one another using a common mycorrhizal network (CMN)—a lattice of fungal strands in the soil. Fernandez and colleagues excluded all pathways other than the CMN by using barriers to keep the plants' root systems separate while allowing mycorrhizal strands through—a crucial step Zhang and colleagues' study did not take.

Text 2

Fernandez and colleagues took the necessary precaution of separating the plants' root systems (thereby excluding root-to-root transmission). However, any barrier used must allow the thread-like hyphae of a CMN to pass through, and this permeability would also allow liquids through. Thus, the researchers' experimental design cannot ensure that any nutrient transfer observed can be attributed to a CMN and not to some other pathway.

Based on the texts, the author of Text 1 and the author of Text 2 would most likely give the same answer to which question?
choices: Is there an available barrier material that can block roots and liquids while allowing fungal strands through?
Did Zhang and colleagues' study effectively exclude any nutrient pathway other than a CMN?
Are the barriers used in Fernandez and colleagues' study sufficient to ensure that nutrient transfer could only occur via a CMN?
Do plants that transfer nutrients through a root-to-root pathway also transmit nutrients via a CMN?
explanation:
What the question is asking

It’s not asking what the authors believe is true about CMNs.

It’s asking:

Which question would both authors give the same answer to?

So we’re looking for something that both texts address or imply in the same way.

What both texts clearly agree on

Root-to-root transfer is a real pathway for nutrient transfer.

Because of that, it must be excluded to study CMN transfer.

Both texts mention root separation as a key experimental concern.

What neither text does:

Claim that root-to-root transfer and CMN transfer are linked or dependent.

Suggest that knowing one tells you anything about the other.

So both authors would answer “We don’t know / not addressed” to questions about whether root-to-root transfer implies CMN transfer.

Why D works

D. “Do plants that transfer nutrients through a root-to-root pathway also transmit nutrients via a CMN?”

Both authors would give the same answer:

This is not something these studies establish.

That shared lack of evidence = same answer.

SAT loves this move: agreement by shared uncertainty.

Why the other choices fail
A

Asks about the existence of a specific barrier material.
Neither text discusses available materials → speculative.

B

About Zhang et al.’s study excluding other pathways.
Text 1 says no. Text 2 doesn’t discuss Zhang at all → not shared.

C

Asks if Fernandez’s barriers are sufficient.
Text 2 says no.
Text 1 implies they’re a crucial improvement → not the same answer.

question:
Text 1

In separate studies, Stephen Meding and Robert J. Zasoski and Xinhua He and colleagues examined whether plants transfer nutrients to one another using a common mycorrhizal network (CMN)—a lattice of fungal strands in the soil. Meding and Zasoski excluded all pathways other than the CMN by using barriers to keep the plants' root systems separate while allowing mycorrhizal strands through—a crucial step He and colleagues' study did not take.

Text 2

Meding and Zasoski took the necessary precaution of separating the plants' root systems (thereby excluding root-to-root transmission). However, any barrier used must allow the thread-like hyphae of a CMN to pass through, and this permeability would also allow liquids through. Thus, the researchers' experimental design cannot ensure that any nutrient transfer observed can be attributed to a CMN and not to some other pathway.

Based on the texts, which choice best describes a point on which the author of Text 1 and the author of Text 2 would most likely agree?
choices: Meding and Zasoski's study effectively excluded any explanation for nutrient transfer other than via a CMN.
Excluding root-to-root transfer of nutrients between plants is sufficient to ensure that any observed nutrient transfer must involve a CMN.
He and colleagues' study was not designed in a way that would allow it to produce compelling evidence that nutrient transfer occurred via a CMN.
A barrier that is impervious to both roots and fungal strands is necessary to evaluate nutrient transfer via a CMN.
explanation:
What Text 1 is saying

Meding and Zasoski did something important: they separated plant roots while still allowing fungal strands (CMN) through.

He and colleagues did not take this step, which makes their study weaker.

So Text 1 implies that He et al.’s design cannot convincingly show CMN-based nutrient transfer.

What Text 2 is saying

Even when roots are separated (as in Meding and Zasoski’s study), barriers that allow fungal strands also allow liquids.

Because of this, nutrients could have moved through some non-CMN pathway.

Therefore, a study like He et al.’s cannot guarantee that observed nutrient transfer happened via a CMN.

Shared point of agreement

Both authors agree that He and colleagues’ study design is insufficient to produce strong evidence that nutrients were transferred via a CMN.

That idea is stated exactly in choice C.

Why the other choices are wrong

A. Says Meding and Zasoski successfully ruled out all other explanations.
Text 2 directly contradicts this by saying other pathways (like liquids) are still possible.

B. Says excluding root-to-root transfer is enough to prove CMN transfer.
Text 2 explicitly says this is not enough.

D. Says barriers must block both roots and fungal strands.
That would make CMN transfer impossible, and neither text suggests this.

question:
Dubautia raillardioides is a species in a family of plants known collectively as the <u>silversword alliance</u>, all of which grow only on the Hawaiian Islands. Members of this alliance exhibit an extraordinary range of phenotypes, with some species maturing into vines and others into shrubs and trees. All species in the alliance descended from a single ancestral tarweed plant that arrived on the islands around 5 million years ago. The tarweed's descendants diversified into distinct species as they adapted to live in the wide variety of habitats found on the Hawaiian Islands.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined phrase in the text as a whole?
choices: It lists species from a family of plants found only on the Hawaiian Islands.
It explains why Dubautia raillardioides is unique among members of the silversword alliance.
It supplies the name used to refer to a group of related plant species.
It provides the common name for the Dubautia raillardioides plant.
explanation:
Step 1: Identify the underlined phrase

The underlined phrase is “the silversword alliance.”

It appears in this sentence:

Dubautia raillardioides is a species in a family of plants known collectively as the silversword alliance…

So the phrase is being used as a label.

Step 2: Ask what job that phrase is doing

The phrase is not:

describing a trait,

explaining uniqueness,

or naming Dubautia raillardioides itself.

Instead, it:

names the broader group that Dubautia raillardioides belongs to.

Everything that follows in the paragraph (shared ancestry, diversification, habitats) refers back to that group.

Step 3: Why C is correct

C. It supplies the name used to refer to a group of related plant species.

That is exactly what “the silversword alliance” does:

It is the collective name for multiple related species

The passage then explains characteristics of that group

Step 4: Why the other choices are wrong

A.
Incorrect because the phrase does not list species—it names the group.

B.
Incorrect because the phrase does not explain why Dubautia raillardioides is unique; it places it within a broader family.

D.
Incorrect because “silversword alliance” is not the common name of Dubautia raillardioides itself, but of the entire group.

question:
The bird species Saltator grossus (the slate-colored grosbeak), which weighs about 45 grams, and Microbates collaris (the collared gnatwren), which weighs about 10 grams, share territory in French Guiana with Thamnomanes caesius (the cinereous antshrike), which emits a loud alarm call when it detects predators. Biologist Ari Martinez and colleagues, who studied the ecological community these species share, hypothesized that since there is an inverse relationship between body size and vulnerability to predation, there will also be an inverse relationship between body size and sensitivity to predator warning signals from neighboring species.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Martinez and colleagues' hypothesis?
choices: When Martinez and colleagues played T. caesius alarm calls, only bird species larger than S. grossus displayed predator avoidance behavior.
M. collaris displayed predator-avoidance behavior when Martinez and colleagues played T. caesius alarm calls as well as when the researchers played control sounds of random noise.
Many bird species smaller than S. grossus displayed predator avoidance behavior in response to T. caesius alarm calls played by Martinez and colleagues, but none smaller than M. collaris did.
M. collaris displayed predator-avoidance behavior in response to T. caesius alarm calls played by Martinez and colleagues, whereas S. grossus did not.
explanation:
Step 1: Restate the hypothesis in simple terms

Martinez and colleagues hypothesize:

Body size and vulnerability to predation are inversely related
smaller birds → more vulnerable
larger birds → less vulnerable

Therefore, body size and sensitivity to alarm calls should also be inversely related
smaller birds → more responsive to alarm calls
larger birds → less responsive

So the prediction is:
smaller species should react to warning calls; larger species should not (or react less).

Step 2: Identify the key species and their sizes

Saltator grossus ≈ 45 g (larger)

Microbates collaris ≈ 10 g (smaller)

Alarm calls come from Thamnomanes caesius

Step 3: Why D directly supports the hypothesis

D.
M. collaris displayed predator-avoidance behavior in response to T. caesius alarm calls, whereas S. grossus did not.

This is exactly what the hypothesis predicts:

Smaller bird (M. collaris) → responds

Larger bird (S. grossus) → does not respond

That is a clean, direct confirmation of an inverse relationship between body size and sensitivity to alarm signals.

Step 4: Why the other choices don’t work

A.
Focuses on species larger than S. grossus responding — the opposite of what’s predicted.

B.
Says M. collaris responds to both alarm calls and random noise.
That undermines the idea that the response is due to predator warnings.

C.
Talks about other species but avoids the key comparison between the two species named in the hypothesis.

question:
The bird species Myiobius barbatus (the bearded flycatcher) shares some territory in French Guiana with Thamnomanes caesius (the cinereous antshrike), which emits a loud alarm call when it detects predators. Biologist Ari Martinez and colleagues recorded T. caesius alarm calls and played them in the vicinity of wild M. barbatus. Finding that the birds often froze in place or scattered into vegetation upon hearing the calls, they concluded that M. barbatus associates T. caesius alarm calls with danger.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Martinez and colleagues' conclusion?
choices: Other bird species than M. barbatus also showed a tendency to freeze in place or scatter into vegetation when Martinez and colleagues played T. caesius alarm calls.
Martinez and colleagues played alarm calls from different T. caesius individuals and observed no significant variation in the responses of M. barbatus.
In some instances, M. barbatus froze in place or scattered into vegetation when Martinez and colleagues approached but before they began playing sounds.
When Martinez and colleagues played control sounds of random noise in the vicinity of M. barbatus, the birds displayed no reaction.
explanation:
Step 1: What is the conclusion?

Martinez and colleagues conclude that:

M. barbatus associates T. caesius alarm calls with danger.

So they are claiming a specific interpretation by the birds:

not just reacting to noise,

but recognizing the alarm call as a warning signal.

Step 2: What kind of evidence would most directly support that?

To support that conclusion, we need to rule out an alternative explanation:

Maybe M. barbatus reacts the same way to any sound, not specifically alarm calls.

So the strongest support would show:

reaction to alarm calls, and

no reaction to sounds that do not signal danger.

Step 3: Why D is correct

D.
When Martinez and colleagues played control sounds of random noise in the vicinity of M. barbatus, the birds displayed no reaction.

This is powerful because it shows:

The birds are not just startled by sound

Their freezing or scattering behavior is specific to T. caesius alarm calls

That directly supports the idea that M. barbatus associates those calls with danger, not with noise in general.

Step 4: Why the other choices don’t directly support the conclusion

A.
Other species reacting doesn’t tell us what M. barbatus understands.

B.
Consistency across different alarm-call individuals shows reliability, but not that the response is tied to danger rather than sound.

C.
This weakens the conclusion by suggesting the birds reacted before hearing the alarm calls.

question:
As complex life cycle parasites, Gonoerca sp. and Clavinema mariae require multiple host species throughout their development. Extrapolating from parasite counts on surf smelt and seven other fish species collected from Puget Sound from 1880 to 2019, Chelsea Wood et al. found that the abundance of three-host parasites, such as Gonoerca sp., negatively correlated with rising average annual sea temperatures; the abundance of two-host parasites, such as C. mariae, was largely stable. Noting that fish and other marine vertebrates are especially vulnerable to climate change, Wood et al. observed that all three-host parasites in the study depend on at least two vertebrate species, while all two-host parasites depend on only one, suggesting that ________.

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: warming-induced population changes among Puget Sound vertebrates may have suppressed some parasite populations, but there were no changes among the eight studied host species that affected two-host parasite abundance.
although Gonoerca sp. and C. mariae both require surf smelt as a host, C. mariae was more adversely affected by warming-driven changes in the surf smelt population than Gonoerca sp. was.
a parasite's sensitivity to warming temperatures is negatively correlated with the number of unique vertebrate species it depends on throughout its life cycle.
population size and density of the eight fish species examined in the study were likely largely unaffected by rising sea temperatures.
explanation:
Step 1: Track the structure of the passage

The passage sets up a pattern → explanation:

Observation

Three-host parasites ↓ as sea temperature ↑

Two-host parasites stayed stable

Key background fact

Fish and other marine vertebrates are especially vulnerable to climate change

Crucial contrast

Three-host parasites depend on at least two vertebrate species

Two-host parasites depend on only one vertebrate species

Conclusion must explain the contrast

Why warming hurts three-host parasites more than two-host parasites

Step 2: What must the completion logically do?

It must:

Connect warming → vertebrate population changes

Explain why parasites needing more vertebrate hosts are more affected

Preserve the fact that two-host parasite abundance stayed stable

Step 3: Why A fits perfectly

A.
Warming-induced population changes among Puget Sound vertebrates may have suppressed some parasite populations, but there were no changes among the eight studied host species that affected two-host parasite abundance.

This does exactly what’s needed:

Explains decline in three-host parasites via host vulnerability

Explains stability of two-host parasites

Uses “may have,” matching the cautious tone (“suggesting that…”)

Step 4: Why the other choices fail

B.
Focuses narrowly on surf smelt and contradicts the claim that C. mariae was stable.

C.
Reverses the relationship: the passage suggests more hosts → more vulnerability, not less.

D.
Contradicts the statement that marine vertebrates are especially vulnerable to climate change.

question:
Chelsea Wood et al. tracked temperature-driven changes in the abundance of Anisakis sp. (a complex life cycle parasite, or CLP, that requires three host species throughout its life cycle), Gyrodactylus sp. (a directly transmitted parasite, which requires only one host species), and 83 other parasite taxa found on eight fish species. CLPs are transmitted when an infected host is ingested by an individual of another species, typically shielding CLPs from the external environment, whereas directly transmitted parasites are exposed to external conditions during transmission. However, Wood et al. found that three-host CLP abundance decreased as sea temperatures rose, whereas directly transmitted parasite abundance was largely stable, suggesting that ________.

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: any advantages that the transmission strategy used by three-host CLPs may have conferred did not completely offset the negative effects of other temperature-driven factors on CLP abundance.
CLPs primarily transmitted by ingestion were less dependent on host species adversely affected by warming temperatures than were CLPs that use other transmission strategies.
as the number of host species involved in a parasite's transmission increases, the parasite is better protected against rising temperatures.
directly transmitted parasites identified in the study were more likely to use transmission strategies that shield them from warming temperatures than were three-host CLPs.
explanation:
Step 1: Identify the apparent contradiction the passage sets up

The passage contrasts two ideas:

Theory / expectation

Three-host CLPs are shielded from external conditions during transmission (they’re inside hosts).

Directly transmitted parasites are exposed to the environment.

Observed result

Three-host CLPs decreased as temperatures rose.

Directly transmitted parasites stayed largely stable.

That’s a mismatch:
the supposedly protected parasites declined more.

So the completion must resolve that contradiction, not reverse it.

Step 2: What must the blank logically say?

It must suggest that:

Even though three-host CLPs should have some protection,

that protection was not enough to overcome other temperature-related harms.

The wording should be cautious and explanatory (suggesting, may have).

Step 3: Why A is correct

A.
any advantages that the transmission strategy used by three-host CLPs may have conferred did not completely offset the negative effects of other temperature-driven factors on CLP abundance.

This fits perfectly because it:

Acknowledges the theoretical advantage (shielding during ingestion),

Explains why the decline still occurred,

Matches the cautious tone (“may have”),

Directly reconciles the evidence.

In short:
Protection exists → but it wasn’t sufficient.

Step 4: Why the other choices fail

B.
Claims CLPs were less dependent on vulnerable hosts — the opposite of what multi-host life cycles imply.

C.
Says more hosts = better protection, which is contradicted by the observed decline.

D.
Claims directly transmitted parasites were more protected, but the passage explicitly says they are more exposed.

question:

Traditionally, certain features of mosque architecture are nearly ______, such as the mihrab (or niche), which almost all mosques include. But mosques can also be built to reflect a multitude of different architectural styles, as in the case of the Great Mosque of Central Java, which includes elements from the Javanese and Greek revival styles.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation:
Correct answer
universal

Why this is correct
The sentence says that certain features of mosque architecture are “nearly ___, such as the mihrab (or niche), which almost all mosques include.”
The key logic is “nearly” + “almost all.” The blank must describe something that is present in almost every case, but not literally every single one.

Universal fits perfectly:
• “Universal” means present everywhere or in almost all cases.
• “Nearly universal” is a very common and precise academic phrase.
• It directly matches “almost all mosques include.”

The second sentence contrasts this idea by saying mosques can still reflect many different architectural styles. That contrast only works if the first idea is about a commonly shared feature.

Why the other choices are wrong

elaborate
• “Elaborate” means detailed or ornate.
• The sentence is not about how decorative the mihrab is; it’s about how commonly it appears.
• “Nearly elaborate” makes no logical or grammatical sense.

illusory
• “Illusory” means false or deceptive.
• That would suggest the mihrab only seems to exist but actually doesn’t, which contradicts “almost all mosques include.”
• This choice directly conflicts with the factual tone of the passage.

idealized
• “Idealized” means represented as perfect or better than reality.
• The sentence is describing an actual architectural feature, not a romanticized or imagined one.
• “Nearly idealized” does not logically connect to inclusion or frequency.

question:
The dates that archaeologists assign to most of the colossal sculptures of human heads produced by the Olmec civilization of Mesoamerica are necessarily ______. The majority of the sculptures have been moved from their original context, making precise dating impossible.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation:
Correct answer
approximate

Why this is correct
The sentence states that archaeologists assign dates to the sculptures, but most of the sculptures have been moved from their original context, “making precise dating impossible.”

The logic is straightforward:
• If precise dating is impossible,
• then the dates cannot be exact,
• therefore the dates must be approximate.

“Necessarily approximate” directly reflects the cause-and-effect relationship in the sentence.

Why the other choices are wrong

uncontroversial
• “Uncontroversial” means not debated or disputed.
• The issue here is accuracy, not disagreement.
• Even if all scholars agreed, the dates could still be imprecise, so this doesn’t address the core problem.

irrelevant
• “Irrelevant” means not related or unimportant.
• Dates are clearly relevant to archaeology; the sentence explains why they are imprecise, not unimportant.
• This choice completely misreads the purpose of the sentence.

applicable
• “Applicable” means relevant or able to be applied.
• The sentence is not questioning whether dates apply; it’s explaining why they can’t be exact.
• This choice fails to connect to “making precise dating impossible.”

question:
______ traditional descriptions of pollination syndromes (suites of floral traits, such as nectar composition and symmetry, hypothesized to have independently evolved as a result of selection pressure exerted by pollinators) and recent empirical observations of floral-trait combinations have led some ecologists to express reservations about the utility of those descriptions.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation:
Correct answer
Discrepancies between

Why this is correct
The sentence structure is:

“_____ traditional descriptions of pollination syndromes … and recent empirical observations of floral-trait combinations have led some ecologists to express reservations about the utility of those descriptions.”

Key logic:
• Traditional descriptions exist.
• Recent empirical observations exist.
• These two things do not line up.
• Because they do not line up, ecologists now question the usefulness of the traditional descriptions.

“Discrepancies between” directly signals a mismatch or conflict between two sets of ideas, which explains why reservations arise.

Grammatically, it also fits perfectly:
“Discrepancies between X and Y have led…”

Why the other choices are wrong

Proclamations of
• “Proclamations” means declarations or announcements.
• The sentence needs a relationship between traditional descriptions and recent observations, not a label for one side alone.
• This choice removes the contrast that explains the ecologists’ reservations.

Recurrences of
• “Recurrences” means repeated appearances of the same thing.
• The passage is not saying old ideas are repeating; it’s saying they conflict with new evidence.
• This choice implies similarity over time, which contradicts the idea of doubt or reservation.

Affinities between
• “Affinities” means similarities or natural connections.
• If there were affinities between the two, ecologists would feel more confident, not less.
• This choice directly contradicts the conclusion of skepticism.

question:
Scientists discovered a 390-million-year-old fossilized forest of Calamophyton trees in modern-day England. The scientists believe the emergence of these Calamophyton forests changed the land significantly. <u>For example, the tree roots would have greatly reduced soil erosion, and the accumulated twigs the trees shed likely created new habitats for animal life.</u>

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It suggests that there are likely fossilized Calamophyton forests from before 390 million years ago.
It provides two competing views of when the Calamophyton forest likely emerged.
It illustrates how Calamophyton forests likely changed conditions on the land.
It indicates how fast the Calamophyton forest spread.
explanation:
Correct answer
It illustrates how Calamophyton forests likely changed conditions on the land.

Why this is correct
The underlined sentence explains mechanisms and effects:

• Tree roots reduced soil erosion.
• Accumulated twigs created new habitats for animal life.

These are concrete examples of how the forest altered land conditions. The sentence is not about timing, speed, or competing theories — it’s about environmental impact.

Thus, its function in the passage is explanatory: showing how those forests changed terrestrial conditions.

Why the other choices are wrong

It suggests that there are likely fossilized Calamophyton forests from before 390 million years ago.
• The sentence says nothing about earlier forests.
• It discusses effects, not fossil evidence or chronology.

It provides two competing views of when the Calamophyton forest likely emerged.
• There is no comparison of theories or timelines.
• No disagreement or debate is presented.

It indicates how fast the Calamophyton forest spread.
• The sentence does not mention speed, expansion, or rate.
• Environmental impact ≠ rate of spread.

question:
The following text is from Louise Erdrich’s 1986 novel The Beet Queen. The narrator discusses her relationship with her young niece, Dot. Celestine, the narrator’s sister-in-law, is Dot’s mother.

Dot and I had a mental connection, I was sure of it. I understood things about the baby that her mother could not accept.

For instance, she was never meant to be a baby.

Dot was as impatient with babyhood as I. She tried at once to grow out of it. Celestine never saw that, because she, and only she, took pleasure in Dot’s helpless softness. Only Celestine was saddened by her daughter’s fierce progress. Day by day, Dot grew stronger. In her shopping-cart stroller she exercised to exhaustion, bouncing for hours to develop her leg muscles.

Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To present the narrator’s belief that she understands Dot better than Celestine does
To speculate that when Dot is older, her personality will be like Celestine’s
To discuss what the narrator and Celestine do to amuse Dot
To compare the narrator’s physical appearance to the physical appearance of Celestine
explanation:
Correct answer
To present the narrator’s belief that she understands Dot better than Celestine does

Why this is correct
The passage consistently centers on the narrator’s perception of Dot and contrasts it—implicitly but clearly—with Celestine’s.

Key logic moves:
• The narrator opens by asserting a “mental connection” with Dot.
• She claims to understand things about Dot that Dot’s mother “could not accept.”
• She frames Dot as fundamentally different from a typical baby (impatient, trying to grow out of babyhood).
• Celestine is portrayed as emotionally affected by Dot’s development, while the narrator positions herself as perceptive and understanding.

The purpose is not to criticize Celestine directly, but to foreground the narrator’s belief that she uniquely understands Dot’s nature.

Why the other choices are wrong

To speculate that when Dot is older, her personality will be like Celestine’s
• The passage focuses on Dot’s infancy, not her future personality.
• There is no speculation about Dot becoming like Celestine; if anything, Dot is contrasted with typical expectations, not aligned with her mother.

To discuss what the narrator and Celestine do to amuse Dot
• No shared actions to entertain Dot are described.
• The stroller detail is observational, not about amusement or caretaking routines.

To compare the narrator’s physical appearance to the physical appearance of Celestine
• There is no physical description of either adult.
• This choice is completely unrelated to the content of the passage.

question:
Adelaide is one of many cities that have installed pontoons or other hardening structures to protect their shorelines against coastal hazards. To assess how birds respond to shoreline hardening and other landscape alterations, Diann Prosser et al. used a tool known as the Index of Waterbird Community Integrity to survey bird communities consisting of sixty-four species, including the tundra swan and the great blue heron, in the Chesapeake Bay on the US East Coast. The researchers concluded that shoreline hardening more negatively affects birds than does land development for uses such as housing.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It introduces a certain technique, mentions the hypothesis of a study into an ecological consequence of that technique, and presents evidence in support of that study’s hypothesis.
It provides an example of a location that has adopted a particular approach, explains the methodology of a study into an ecological effect of that approach, and describes a finding of that study.
It makes a claim about the use of a specific strategy, describes field observations of a consequence of that strategy in a particular ecosystem, and makes a supposition based on those observations.

It presents a solution to a commonly occurring problem, summarizes the procedures used by a group of researchers studying the environmental impact of that solution, and notes the significance of the researchers’ findings.
explanation:
Correct answer
It provides an example of a location that has adopted a particular approach, explains the methodology of a study into an ecological effect of that approach, and describes a finding of that study.

Why this is correct
The passage has a clear three-part structure:

Context / example
• Adelaide is introduced as a city that has installed shoreline hardening structures.

Study and methodology
• Researchers developed a tool (the Index of Waterbird Community Integrity).
• They surveyed bird communities across multiple sites and species.

Findings
• The researchers concluded that shoreline hardening has more negative effects on birds than land development.

Choice B matches this progression precisely: example → method → finding.

Why the other choices are wrong

It introduces a certain technique, mentions the hypothesis of a study into an ecological consequence of that technique, and presents evidence in support of that study’s hypothesis.
• The passage does not explicitly state a hypothesis.
• It reports a conclusion, not a tested prediction followed by supporting evidence.

It makes a claim about the use of a specific strategy, describes field observations of a consequence of that strategy in a particular ecosystem, and makes a supposition based on those observations.
• The conclusion is presented as a researched finding, not a tentative supposition.
• The wording understates the certainty of the researchers’ conclusion.

It presents a solution to a commonly occurring problem, summarizes the procedures used by a group of researchers studying the environmental impact of that solution, and notes the significance of the researchers’ findings.
• Shoreline hardening is not framed as a solution being advocated.
• The passage does not emphasize the significance or broader implications—only the result.

question:
Women like Dorothy T. Blum made important early contributions to the history of US cryptology, a field concerned with secure data communication and storage. Blum provided cryptological services for the US Army in the 1940s and then joined the National Security Agency (NSA). She was a pioneer in transitioning the NSA to using computers for cryptanalysis. In this way, Blum and others like her helped make it possible for more women—such as Maureen Baginski, who currently works in intelligence and supports the FBI—to enter the field of cryptology.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Cryptology is a field that focuses primarily on securely managing data.
Women such as Dorothy T. Blum and Maureen Baginski have contributed to the field of cryptology.
Dorothy T. Blum and Maureen Baginski worked together on an important project in the field of cryptology.
Cryptology should be taught more often in schools to encourage more women to enter the field.
explanation:
Correct answer
Women such as Dorothy T. Blum and Maureen Baginski have contributed to the field of cryptology.

Why this is correct
The passage’s main focus is on women’s contributions to cryptology, using Dorothy T. Blum as the primary example and Maureen Baginski as a later figure whose career was made possible, in part, by earlier pioneers like Blum.

Core logic:
• The opening sentence establishes women’s early contributions to U.S. cryptology.
• The passage details Blum’s specific work and influence.
• It ends by showing how that influence helped open the field to other women, including Baginski.

This choice captures the central, recurring idea of the passage without adding claims or narrowing the focus too much.

Why the other choices are wrong

Cryptology is a field that focuses primarily on securely managing data.
• This is background information, not the passage’s main idea.
• The passage is about people and contributions, not a definition of cryptology.

Dorothy T. Blum and Maureen Baginski worked together on an important project in the field of cryptology.
• The passage never says they worked together.
• Baginski is mentioned as a later beneficiary of earlier progress, not a collaborator.

Cryptology should be taught more often in schools to encourage more women to enter the field.
• This is a prescriptive recommendation.
• The passage is descriptive and historical, not argumentative or policy-driven.

question:
Researchers who examined data from radio-tagged southern sea otters (Enhydra lutris nereis) identified fitness benefits gained by otters that used tools. By using fixed stones as anvils, tool-using otters gained access to high-quality, hard-shelled prey (e.g., mussels and clams) that they could usually not access through biting alone. Non-tool-using otters foraged abundant, energy-poor, easily extractable prey instead (e.g., snails). Even when easily processed prey were depleted, tool-using otters that processed mussels and clams were thus able to obtain their needed energy resources and to do so without incurring tooth damage.

What does the text most strongly suggest about southern sea otters in environments where snails, mussels, and clams are present?
choices: Those otters whose diet consists mainly of snails will likely exhibit less tooth damage than will those otters that use tools to consume mussels and clams.
Those otters that do not use tools will likely have more robust health than those otters that do use tools.
Those otters that do not use tools will likely need to process larger amounts of prey to meet their energy requirements than will those otters that use tools.
Those otters that consume mussels and clams without the use of tools will likely spend less time foraging than will those otters that use tools to access the same prey resources.
explanation:
Logic.
Combine the passage facts and determine which conclusion follows without adding a new assumption. The facts imply that those otters that do not use tools will likely need to process larger amounts of prey to meet their energy requirements than will those otters that use tools. This conclusion follows from the stated evidence while the other choices add or contradict information.

Correct answer. C.
C. This choice is correct because the passage establishes that even when easily processed prey were depleted tool-using otters that processed mussels and clams were thus able to obtain their needed energy resources and to do so without incurring tooth damage and this makes it reasonable to infer that those otters that do not use tools will likely need to process larger amounts of prey to meet their energy requirements than will those otters that use tools.

Incorrect answers.
A. This choice is incorrect because the statement that those otters whose diet consists mainly of snails will likely exhibit less tooth damage than will those otters that use tools to consume mussels and clams does not provide the evidence required by the passage.
B. This choice is incorrect because the statement that those otters that do not use tools will likely have more robust health than those otters that do use tools does not provide the evidence required by the passage.
D. This choice is incorrect because the statement that those otters that consume mussels and clams without the use of tools will likely spend less time foraging than will those otters that use tools to access the same prey resources does not provide the evidence required by the passage.

question:
Over the course of the 1900s, more and more Native Hawaiians spoke English instead of the Hawaiian language. To preserve their language, Native Hawaiian teachers founded the ʻAha Pūnana Leo preschool in 1984. They spoke Hawaiian while teaching, and their Native Hawaiian students were soon able to understand and speak it themselves. The school was a huge success. Eventually it opened locations around Hawaiʻi and started teaching Hawaiian to elementary and high school students too. <u>Thanks to ʻAha Pūnana Leo, the number of young people who speak the language has increased.</u>

Which statement, if true, would most directly support the underlined claim?
choices: Besides Native Hawaiians, tens of thousands of people from other Pacific Islander communities live in Hawaiʻi today, including over 37,000 Samoans.
Fewer than fifty children could speak Hawaiian when ʻAha Pūnana Leo was founded, but now more than 2,000 students at ʻAha Pūnana Leo speak it.
Hawaiian is very similar to other languages that are spoken on the Polynesian Islands of the Pacific Ocean, including Tahitian, Samoan, and Māori.
Roughly 680,000 Native Hawaiian people lived in the United States in 2020, and a little less than half of them lived in Hawaiʻi.
explanation:
Logic.
State the passage claim as a testable prediction before comparing the choices. The needed evidence must show that fewer than fifty children could speak Hawaiian when ʻAha Pūnana Leo was founded but now more than 2 000 students at ʻAha Pūnana Leo speak it. This result directly strengthens the claim while the other choices do not test it.

Correct answer. B.
B. This choice is correct because the evidence that fewer than fifty children could speak Hawaiian when ʻAha Pūnana Leo was founded but now more than 2 000 students at ʻAha Pūnana Leo speak it confirms the passage point that thanks to ʻAha Pūnana Leo the number of young people who speak the language has increased.

Incorrect answers.
A. This choice is incorrect because the statement that besides Native Hawaiians tens of thousands of people from other Pacific Islander communities live in Hawaiʻi today including over 37 000 Samoans does not provide the evidence required by the passage.
C. This choice is incorrect because the statement that hawaiian is very similar to other languages that are spoken on the Polynesian Islands of the Pacific Ocean including Tahitian Samoan and Māori does not provide the evidence required by the passage.
D. This choice is incorrect because the statement that roughly 680 000 Native Hawaiian people lived in the United States in 2020 and a little less than half of them lived in Hawaiʻi does not provide the evidence required by the passage.

question:
Cumulative Counts of Fish in Three Taiwanese Tide Pools, 1999–2018

Species | Station 1 | Station 2 | Station 3

question:

In Oz, “Dorothy fell asleep only once, and then she dreamed she was in Kansas, where Aunt Em was telling her how glad she was to have her little girl at home again.”
In Kansas, “Dorothy lived in the midst of the great Kansas prairies, with Uncle Henry, who was a farmer, and Aunt Em, who was the farmer’s wife.”
In Kansas, “When Dorothy stood in the doorway and looked around, she could see nothing but the great gray prairie on every side. Not a tree nor a house broke the broad sweep of flat country.”
explanation:
Correct answer
“In Kansas, ‘When Dorothy stood in the doorway and looked around, she could see nothing but the great gray prairie on every side. Not a tree nor a house broke the broad sweep of flat country.’”

The claim to be illustrated is that Dorothy’s aunt and uncle’s house in Kansas is remote and solitary.

• Highlighting the vast, empty prairie
• Creating a strong sense of isolation

• It does not address remoteness or solitude.

• This is about longing or memory, not isolation.
• It does not describe the setting of Kansas.

“In Kansas, ‘Dorothy lived in the midst of the great Kansas prairies…’”
• This provides general location information.

question:
Carcinization, or the evolution of a crablike body form, has taken place in crustaceans many times over the last 250 million years. Decarcinization has occurred several times as well, even though it involves the loss of traits such as sideways walking that seem to have helped carcinized groups persist in a variety of ecosystems. In a 2021 paper, Joanna Wolfe and team note that many decarcinized groups are extinct and have very few living relatives—signs that decarcinization might be an “evolutionary dead-end.” But the team also discusses frog crabs, a living decarcinized group with traits suited to dwelling in sediment; fossils show that the group had decarcinized members as far back as the Early Cretaceous. This example suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the evolutionary benefits of a crablike body form are less certain than many studies of carcinization had previously implied.
despite having many living relatives, some decarcinized groups did not benefit from decarcinization.
sideways walking may have been less important to the survival of frog crabs than a protected abdomen and other traits associated with carcinization.
a crablike body form may not be optimal in all cases, with ecological conditions sometimes favoring the persistence of decarcinization.
explanation:
Logic.
State the passage claim as a testable prediction before comparing the choices. The needed evidence must show that a crablike body form may not be optimal in all cases with ecological conditions sometimes favoring the persistence of decarcinization. This result directly strengthens the claim while the other choices do not test it.

Correct answer. D.
D. This choice is correct because the claim that ______ is strengthened by the finding that a crablike body form may not be optimal in all cases with ecological conditions sometimes favoring the persistence of decarcinization.

Incorrect answers.
A. This choice is incorrect because the statement that the evolutionary benefits of a crablike body form are less certain than many studies of carcinization had previously implied does not provide the evidence required by the passage.
B. This choice is incorrect because the statement that despite having many living relatives some decarcinized groups did not benefit from decarcinization does not provide the evidence required by the passage.
C. This choice is incorrect because the statement that sideways walking may have been less important to the survival of frog crabs than a protected abdomen and other traits associated with carcinization does not provide the evidence required by the passage.

Correct answer

question:
Studying menus from nineteenth-century restaurants, old coupons clipped out of newspapers, and posters promoting concerts by long-forgotten musicians may seem like a frivolous pursuit, but ephemeral objects like these are useful as evidence of cultural change: they can _____ shifts in norms, values, and concerns that traditional objects of historical inquiry may not.

explanation:
Correct answer
attest to

Why this is correct
The sentence argues that studying seemingly trivial, ephemeral objects can serve as evidence of cultural change. The phrase needed must mean “provide evidence for” or “bear witness to.”

“Attest to” fits perfectly:
• It means to confirm, demonstrate, or provide evidence of something.
• “Objects … attest to shifts in norms, values, and concerns” is a precise academic phrasing.

Why the other choices are wrong

dissociate from
• Means to separate or distance from.
• This reverses the intended meaning; the objects are connected to cultural change, not separated from it.

collude with
• Means to secretly cooperate, often illegally.
• Completely inappropriate in both tone and meaning.

compensate for
• Means to make up for a deficiency.
• The sentence is not about offsetting a lack, but about evidentiary value.

question:
Some ethicists challenge the concept of personal character, claiming that if it were meaningful, situational factors could not, as they clearly can, induce behavior contrary to that character. As Rachana Kamtekar observes, this argument is difficult to reconcile with our lay conception of character: we expect a person of helpful character to be frequently helpful, not _____ helpful.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation:
Correct answer
unfailingly

Why this is correct
The sentence argues against a situational view of character by asserting a consistent pattern of behavior.

Logic:
• A helpful person should be helpful frequently.
• And crucially, not occasionally unhelpful.

“Unfailingly” means always, without exception:
• “Frequently helpful, not unfailingly helpful” creates a clear, logical contrast.
• It supports the idea that even good character allows occasional lapses.

Why the other choices are wrong

self-servingly
• Means acting in one’s own interest.
• Does not contrast with “frequently helpful.”

sporadically
• Means occasionally or irregularly.
• This weakens the contrast and reverses the logic.

grudgingly
• Means reluctantly.
• Describes attitude, not consistency.

question:

• The focus is institutional atypicality, not curatorial reasoning.

question:
The Heege Manuscript (HM) is a collection of booklets of once-unbound paper sheets on which Richard Heege copied various texts at his fifteenth-century home between Derbyshire and Nottinghamshire in England. <u>Most other contemporaneous personal manuscripts like the Findern Anthology (FA) consist primarily of pieces by celebrated medieval authors like Hoccleve and other readings favored by elites</u>, whereas the HM has a distinctive emphasis on the popular, including entertainments like crude comedies, and the practical, with advice about manners.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
choices: To suggest that the FA is a poor point of comparison for a collection like the HM
To emphasize the ubiquity of hand-copied collections like the FA and the HM in medieval England
To provide context for the text’s suggestion that the HM is an outlier among collections of its time
To illustrate how the discussion of the HM earlier in the text can improve historians’ understanding of the FA
explanation:
Correct answer
To provide context for the text’s suggestion that the HM is an outlier among collections of its time

Why this is correct
The underlined portion describes the Finder Anthology (FA) before contrasting it with the Heege Manuscript (HM).

Logical role of the underlined text:
• Establishes what typical collections of the time emphasized
• Makes it possible to see how HM differs (popular entertainment, practical advice)

Thus, the underlined text sets up a baseline, allowing the HM to stand out as unusual.

Why the other choices are wrong

To suggest that the FA is a poor point of comparison for a collection like the HM
• The FA is actually used as a useful comparison.
• The passage relies on the FA to highlight contrast.

To emphasize the ubiquity of hand-copied collections like the FA and the HM in medieval England
• The focus is on content, not prevalence.
• Ubiquity is not discussed.

To illustrate how the discussion of the HM earlier in the text can improve historians’ understanding of the FA
• The direction of explanation is reversed.
• The FA is used to explain the HM, not the other way around.

question:
Text 1 is T.E. Hulme’s 1912 poem “Above the Dock.” Text 2 is from Amy Lowell’s 1912 poem “The Crescent Moon.”

Text 1

Above the quiet dock in mid night,
Tangled in the tall mast’s corded height,
Hangs the moon. What seemed so far away
Is but a child’s balloon, forgotten after play.

Text 2

Slipping softly through the sky
Little horned, happy moon,
Can you hear me up so high?
Will you come down soon?

Which choice best describes a notable difference in how the speaker of Text 1 and the speaker of Text 2 portray the moon?
choices: While both speakers characterize the moon as an entrapped figure, only the speaker of Text 2 describes the moon as being content with this fate.
While both speakers present the moon as a tangible object, only the speaker of Text 1 addresses the moon’s beauty.
While the speaker of Text 1 presents the moon as an object of play, the speaker of Text 2 presents the moon as an object of serious study.
While the speaker of Text 1 presents the moon as seeming to be very close, the speaker of Text 2 emphasizes the moon’s distance from the speaker.

question:
Mauricio Drelichman and Hans-Joachim Voth’s research into the debt defaults of Philip II (who ruled an empire including Spain and much of Belgium from 1556 to 1598) relates to other work on European early modern state finance, including Hoffman and Norberg’s research on the relationship between state finance and political development. But Drelichman and Voth’s unique contribution to the field is their reconstruction of the earliest extant set of annual fiscal records for any sovereign state, demonstrating in turn that Philip’s defaults were caused by short-term cash shortages, not long-term unsustainable debts.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Analysis of the earliest available records of a sovereign state’s finances can be found not in the work of Hoffman and Norberg but in that of Drelichman and Voth.
Drelichman and Voth advanced the field of research on European early modern state finance by assembling a novel collection of evidence that gave them insight into Philip II’s debt defaults.
The research by Drelichman and Voth suggests that the logistics of ruling both Spain and much of Belgium led to short-term problems with cash that forced Philip II to default on his debts.
Drelichman and Voth’s research on Philip II’s debt defaults builds on earlier work by Hoffman and Norberg, adding nuance to the earlier work’s findings.
explanation:
Correct answer
Drelichman and Voth advanced the field of research on European early modern state finance by assembling a novel collection of evidence that gave them insight into Philip II’s debt defaults.

Why this is correct
The passage emphasizes:
• Their use of newly uncovered financial records
• How those records allowed a better explanation of Philip II’s defaults
• How their work goes beyond earlier research

Choice B captures both the method (novel evidence) and the contribution (new insight).

Why the other choices are wrong

Analysis of the earliest available records…can be found not in Hoffman and Norberg but in Drelichman and Voth.
• This overstates exclusivity.
• The passage does not say earlier scholars lacked such analysis entirely.

The research by Drelichman and Voth suggests that the logistics of ruling…led to short-term problems…
• This is too narrow.
• It omits the methodological contribution emphasized in the text.

Drelichman and Voth’s research…builds on earlier work…adding nuance…
• While true, this understates the novelty and significance of their contribution.

question:
The following text is adapted from William Shakespeare’s 1597 play The Tragedy of King Richard III. Richard is reflecting on the recent arrest of his brother, the Duke of Clarence, on suspicion of treason against King Edward IV. Derby, Hastings, Buckingham, Rivers, Dorset, and Grey are also members of the English nobility.

RICHARD: I do the wrong, and first begin to brawl.
The secret mischiefs that I set [flowing]
I lay unto the grievous charge of others.
Clarence, whom I indeed have cast in darkness,
I do beweep to many simple [gullible people],
Namely, to Derby, Hastings, Buckingham;
And tell them ’tis the Queen and her allies
That stir the King against the Duke my brother.
Now they believe it, and withal whet me
To be revenged on Rivers, Dorset, Grey.

Which choice best describes what happens in the text?
choices: Richard attributes Clarence’s troubles to both his own secret plotting and the distrust of Clarence that the queen and her allies Derby, Hastings, and Buckingham have planted in the king’s mind.

Richard describes having wept as he informed Derby, Hastings, and Buckingham that the queen and her allies convinced the king to act against Clarence, and says that the earnestness of his grief caused them to accept his version of events.

Richard acknowledges that his mischievous nature has spurred him to commit misdeeds in the past, including instigating enmity between the king and Clarence, but he reports that he has hitherto not lost the trust of the queen and her allies.

Richard indicates that he has pretended to be aggrieved about Clarence’s situation and has proclaimed it to be the fault of the queen and her allies, but in reality, he has caused the hostility the king feels toward Clarence.
explanation:
Here’s a clear, line-by-line interpretation in modern English:

I do the wrong, and first begin to brawl.
I am the one who commits the wrongdoing and starts the conflict.

The secret mischiefs that I set flowing
The hidden schemes and trouble that I put into motion

I lay unto the grievous charge of others.
I blame those serious crimes on other people.

Clarence, whom I indeed have cast in darkness,
Clarence, whom I have truly caused to be imprisoned and ruined,

I do beweep to many simple [gullible people],
I pretend to mourn and feel sorrow in front of naïve, easily fooled people,

Namely, to Derby, Hastings, Buckingham;
Specifically, to Derby, Hastings, and Buckingham.

And tell them ’tis the Queen and her allies
And I tell them it is the queen and the people aligned with her

That stir the King against the Duke my brother.
Who have provoked the king into turning against my brother, the Duke of Clarence.

Now they believe it, and withal whet me
Now they believe this lie, and at the same time they urge and encourage me

To be revenged on Rivers, Dorset, Grey.
To take revenge on Rivers, Dorset, and Grey.

Richard is openly admitting to the audience that he himself engineered Clarence’s arrest, but he is pretending to be sad about it in public. He says he “weeps” to gullible nobles (Derby, Hastings, Buckingham) and lies, telling them that the queen and her allies are to blame. Those nobles believe him and, as a result, encourage Richard to seek revenge on the queen’s allies. In short: Richard caused the problem, then blamed others while acting innocent.

Why this is correct

Choice D highlights the largest contrast, making it the most striking and effective completion.

question:
In what is now southern Florida, the Calusa people (circa 1000–1600 CE) supported their relatively large population’s dietary needs with hydrological engineering rather than terrestrial farming methods. They constructed watercourts (gated coastal enclosures) out of shells and sediments to trap a variety of fish as waters rose and fell with tides and seasonal sea-level shifts; watercourt pools then held the fish for later consumption. Archaeologist Theresa Schober has posited an additional purpose of these enclosures, suggesting that they were intended to foster conch. She ties this hypothesis to the high value the sea snails would have had for the Calusa, both nutritionally and as a building material (conch shells are highly durable).

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Schober’s hypothesis?
choices: Samples of animal remains collected at Calusa sites reflect a greater diversity of marine species, particularly among sea snails, within the perimeter of watercourts than in locations known to have been devoted to the preparation and consumption of food.

Historical population-size estimates suggest that the sea snails and fish most common in the Calusa diet were plentiful in open coastal waters when the watercourts were constructed but decreased in abundance in the years immediately after construction.

Radar surveys of Calusa sites reveal watercourt dimensions suitable for sustaining fish of many local species but not conducive for maintaining the shallow environments with ample seagrasses that allow sea snails to thrive.

Sediment layers excavated from Calusa watercourt sites contain heterogeneous mixtures of scales from multiple species of fish and fragments of shells from various types of sea snails, but conch shells do not constitute the majority of the mixture in most of those layers.
explanation:
Correct answer
Radar surveys of Calusa sites reveal watercourt dimensions suitable for sustaining fish of many local species but not conducive for maintaining the shallow environments with ample seagrasses that allow sea snails to thrive.

Why this is correct
Schober’s hypothesis claims that the Calusa built watercourts partly to harvest sea snails, implying that the structures were well suited to snail habitats. A finding that the watercourts were not conducive to sea-snail-friendly environments directly undermines that purpose.

This is a classic mechanism challenge: if the structures could not support sea snails, then the hypothesis about their snail-harvesting function is weakened.

Why the other choices are wrong

Samples of animal remains reflect greater diversity of marine species among sea snails.
• This supports the idea that snails were important nutritionally.
• It strengthens, not weakens, the hypothesis.

Historical population estimates show snails decreased after construction.
• This could suggest overharvesting, not lack of purpose.
• It does not challenge the original intention of building watercourts.

Sediment layers contain mixed remains with shells not in the majority.
• Shells need not dominate sediment to be valuable as food or building material.
• This is inconclusive, not directly weakening.

question:
Observed Traits in a Population of Broadleaf Arrowhead, by Flowering Date

Trait | Day 5 | Day 10 | Day 15 | Day 20
Total number of open male and female per growth unit | 25 | 65 | 110 | 45
Estimated reproductive success rate of male flowers | 0.29 | 0.29 | 0.29 | 0.29
Proportion of male flowers | 0.45 | 0.50 | 0.48 | 0.13

The mating environment hypothesis predicts that populations of flowering plants compensate for reduced mating opportunities due to dichogamy (a plant’s expression of male and female functions at separate times) by increasing the bias of floral sex allocation during the flowering period, increasing the probability of successful cross-pollination. Researchers tested the hypothesis by examining a population of broadleaf arrowhead, a plant for which bloom onset generally takes longer for male flowers than for female flowers, during the flowering season. They concluded that the mating environment hypothesis is not well supported by their observational data.

Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researchers’ conclusion?
choices: Whereas the total number of open flowers per growth unit peaked on day 15, the proportion of male flowers experienced a peak earlier in the flowering season, on day 10.
Despite the sharp reduction in the total number of open flowers per growth unit from day 15 to 20, there was no decline in the estimated reproductive success rate of male flowers in that interval.
Sex allocations were largely evenly distributed on days 10 and 15 but were female biased on days 5 and 20.
Although sex allocations became overwhelmingly female biased by day 20, male flowers’ estimated reproductive success rate did not vary from day 5 to 20.
explanation:
First, restate the hypothesis being tested
The mating environment hypothesis predicts that when mating opportunities are reduced (because male and female functions occur at different times), plants should shift sex allocation during flowering in a way that increases successful cross-pollination.
So if the hypothesis were supported, we would expect changes in the proportion of male flowers to be associated with changes in male reproductive success.

Now look at the key data patterns in the table

Proportion of male flowers

Day 5: 0.45

Day 10: 0.50

Day 15: 0.48

Day 20: 0.13

By day 20, sex allocation becomes strongly female-biased (very low proportion of male flowers).

Estimated reproductive success rate of male flowers

Day 5: 0.29

Day 10: 0.29

Day 15: 0.29

Day 20: 0.29

Male reproductive success does not change at all, despite major changes in sex allocation.

Why this undermines the hypothesis
If shifting sex allocation were compensating for reduced mating opportunities, then changing the proportion of male flowers should affect male reproductive success. But the data show that even when male flowers become rare (day 20), their reproductive success remains unchanged. That means the allocation shift is not improving mating outcomes, which weakens the hypothesis.

Now evaluate the choices

Choice A
This only describes timing differences in peaks. It does not address reproductive success, so it does not support rejecting the hypothesis.

Choice B
This focuses on flower number versus reproductive success, not sex allocation bias. It doesn’t address the hypothesis directly.

Choice C
This incorrectly states that days 5 and 20 were female-biased. Day 5 is near even, not female-biased.

Choice D
This correctly captures the key contradiction:
Even though sex allocation becomes overwhelmingly female-biased by day 20, male reproductive success stays constant from day 5 through day 20. That directly supports the researchers’ conclusion that the hypothesis is not well supported.

Correct answer: D

Big takeaway
The strongest evidence against the mating environment hypothesis is that dramatic shifts in sex allocation do not lead to any improvement or change in male reproductive success.

question:
Although Grant Tavinor concludes that computer games are art by virtue of their forming a subcategory of fiction, and Berys Gaut similarly places them within the realm of cinema, neither approach adequately captures a central aspect of playing these games: when the player no longer attends to the narrative and is instead simply absorbed in the instrumentalities of gameplay. This is among the reasons philosopher C. Thi Nguyen contends that the work of computer game designers is in what he calls the medium of player agency, which the designer prescribes through rules and goals, and which elicits positive aesthetic experiences in the player who agrees to adopt it. Therefore, Nguyen’s position is that Tavinor’s and Gaut’s frameworks ___

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: are helpful starting points for studying computer games as art, even though these frameworks are overly simplistic.
are useful for analyzing the narrative aspects of computer games, even if neither attempts to address player agency.
overstate the influence of fiction and cinema on the narrative elements of computer games.
subsume computer games under other categories of media that do not address a feature of games that is integral to player enjoyment.
explanation:
Correct answer
subsumes computer games under other categories of media that do not address a feature of games that is integral to player enjoyment.

Why this is correct
Nguyen criticizes frameworks that treat games like fiction or cinema because they ignore player agency, which he argues is central to how games produce enjoyment.

Choice D directly captures this criticism: those frameworks misclassify games and fail to address an essential feature.

Why the other choices are wrong

Helpful starting points but overly simplistic.
• Nguyen explicitly argues they are inadequate, not merely simplistic.

Useful for analyzing narrative aspects.
• The criticism is broader than narrative; it concerns agency.

Overstate influence of fiction and cinema.
• This misrepresents the critique; influence is not the issue.

question:
As observed in a 2011 study by Emilio García-Robledo and Alfonso Corzo, macroalgal proliferation may have a suppressive effect on the abundance of cyanobacteria and other microphytobenthos (MPB)—chlorophyll-producing microbes inhabiting marine sediment—in part by reducing the amount of sunlight available to MPB. Examining benthic chlorophyll concentrations (a widely used proxy for MPB biomass) in mudflats in Curlew Bay and other coastal sites in Virginia, Alice F. Besterman and Michael L. Pace found that those concentrations did not negatively correlate with macroalgal proliferation. However, they noted that MPB may respond to low-light conditions by producing higher-than-normal concentrations of chlorophyll, and they thus concluded that ______.

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: researchers ought to account for the possibility that because MPB have the capacity to compensate for reduced sunlight availability, benthic chlorophyll concentrations may not always be a reliable indicator of MPB biomass.

although their finding was inconsistent with that of García-Robledo and Corzo, this discrepancy was not attributable to the ability of MPB to accelerate chlorophyll production to mitigate the negative impact of macroalgal accumulations.

although elevated levels of macroalgae do not always correspond to increased levels of benthic chlorophyll, there is likely a larger trend in MPB biomass that is related to macroalgal presence but unrelated to light conditions.

the effect of macroalgal concentrations on MPB abundance that García-Robledo and Corzo reported was not observed in Curlew Bay and other Virginia sites because low-light conditions likely are not generalizable across the sites in the studies.
explanation:
Correct answer
researchers ought to account for the possibility that because MPB have the capacity to compensate for reduced sunlight availability, benthic chlorophyll concentrations may not always be a reliable indicator of MPB biomass.

Why this is correct
The researchers observe that MPB can produce extra chlorophyll under low-light conditions, meaning chlorophyll levels may not directly reflect biomass.

This is a measurement-validity conclusion: the indicator may be misleading under certain conditions.

Why the other choices are wrong

Discrepancy not attributable to MPB ability.
• Contradicts the passage’s explicit explanation.

Larger trend unrelated to light.
• Unsupported generalization.

Low-light conditions not generalizable.
• The issue is measurement reliability, not site generalization.

question:
Neuroscientist Artin Arshamian and his team sought to determine what affects a person’s perception of an odor as pleasant: is it culture, personal taste, or aspects of human anatomy? The team assessed odor preferences in ten groups of people with different modes of living (urban, agricultural, and hunter-gatherer) including the Maniq people from a small community in Thailand and the Seri people from a small community in Mexico. The team observed that across cultures, people generally rated odors about the same: ethyl butyrate, which smells like peaches, was typically rated more pleasant than diethyl disulfide, which smells like garlic. The team’s study thus undermined the idea that ______.

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: a person who perceives certain odors as pleasant will likely perceive the odors as roughly equal in pleasantness.
culture significantly influences whether a person perceives an odor as pleasant or unpleasant.
personal taste has little influence on whether odors are perceived as pleasant or unpleasant.
people agree in their perception of odors as pleasant or unpleasant regardless of where they live.
explanation:
Correct answer
culture significantly influences whether a person perceives an odor as pleasant or unpleasant.

Why this is correct
The study found cross-cultural agreement on odor pleasantness, which undermines the idea that odor perception is primarily shaped by personal taste or cultural background.

Thus, the conclusion is that culture does not strongly determine pleasantness judgments—making choice B the claim that is undermined.

Why the other choices are wrong

People perceive odors as equally pleasant.
• Too absolute and not stated.

Personal taste has little influence.
• The study addresses culture, not individual taste.

People agree regardless of location.
• Overgeneralizes beyond the study’s scope.

question:
Many studies have found a positive association between levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury in bodies of fresh water undisturbed by human activity. But Stéphane Guédron, Delphine Tisserand, and colleagues did not find this correlation in an examination of freshwater bodies impacted by wastewater. However, Ida Tjermjen and colleagues carried out a study on freshwater bodies disturbed by urban development that showed similar results to the studies on undisturbed waters, suggesting that ______.

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury are both much higher in bodies of fresh water impacted by wastewater than in bodies of fresh water disturbed by urban development.
Guédron, Tisserand, and colleagues’ study used different methods to measure the concentration of mercury in fresh water than Tjerngren and colleagues’ study did.
the effects of wastewater on the association between levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury should not be taken as indicative of the effects of every type of human disturbance.
disturbances linked to wastewater affect significantly more bodies of fresh water than disturbances linked to urban development do.
explanation:
Correct answer
the effects of wastewater on the association between levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury should not be taken as indicative of the effects of every type of human disturbance.

Why this is correct
The passage shows that different disturbances produce different results:
• Wastewater-impacted waters: no correlation
• Urban development: correlation persists

Thus, conclusions drawn from one disturbance type should not be generalized to all.

Why the other choices are wrong

Levels are higher in wastewater-impacted waters.
• Not stated.

Different measurement methods.
• No evidence of methodological differences.

Wastewater affects more bodies of water.
• Irrelevant to the logic of the conclusion.

question:

As part of his I GOT UP series, Japanese conceptual artist On Kawara spent over a decade— with near daily consistency—mailing postcards to friends declaring what time he got up each day, resulting in pieces such as I Got Up at 7:19 A.M., June 6 1977. Such meticulous documentation of mundane ______ artworks that “resonate with existential, psychological and scientific implications about the time-space continuum,” according to the New York Times, became Kawara’s life’s work.

For her film I Am Somebody (1970), a documentary about a successful months-long strike held by Black female hospital workers in Charleston, South Carolina, director Madeline Anderson chose a narrator who had participated in the ______ by allowing the narrative to be shaped by one of their own, amplified the agency and power the workers possessed.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

At a time when many women writers used male pseudonyms to gain greater freedom of self-expression by evading gender conventions, Katherine Bradley and Edith Cooper adapted the practice by publishing poetry, prose, and drama for four decades under the shared name Michael Field. ______ the duo was able to express the joint creative vision that sustained their long personal and professional partnership.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Correct answer

Why this is correct

• cause → effect

Why the other choices are wrong

For instance,

Later,

On the other hand,

question:
In a 2005 study by Mellado et al., the researchers’ aim was to analyze the diet composition of cattle in Coahuila, Mexico. ______ they aimed to analyze the ratio of three different plant subtypes within these animals’ diet: graminoids, forbs, and browse.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Correct answer
Specifically,

Why this is correct
The first clause states the general aim of the study (to analyze diet composition).
The second clause narrows that aim to exactly what was analyzed (the ratio of three plant subtypes).

“Specifically” correctly signals a move from general to detailed information.

Why the other choices are wrong

Instead,
• Signals replacement or opposition.
• No contrast exists.

All the same,
• Signals concession.
• No tension or contradiction exists.

Therefore,
• Signals a conclusion.
• The sentence provides clarification, not inference.

question:
John Quincy Adams employed the pseudonym “Marcellus”—a reference to a leader of an ancient Roman army—in political essays he wrote in 1793, a choice that accomplished far more than simply concealing his authorship. ______ it wasn’t an arbitrary pen name but rather a complex rhetorical strategy through which Adams aligned his political views with the venerated republican ideals of the ancient world, thereby bolstering the authority of his writing.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Correct answer
Indeed,

Why this is correct
The sentence explains that Adams’s pseudonym was not arbitrary, and the following clause reinforces that claim by explaining its symbolic significance.

“Indeed” works as an emphasis and confirmation marker, strengthening the preceding idea.

Why the other choices are wrong

Conversely,
• Signals contrast.
• The ideas align, not oppose.

In addition,
• Signals simple addition.
• The relationship is explanatory emphasis, not mere addition.

However,
• Signals contradiction.
• No contradiction exists.

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Kale is a vegetable that contains ascorbic acid, an essential nutrient for humans.
• Apricots are fruits that contain ascorbic acid.
• There is 120 milligrams (mg) of ascorbic acid per every 100 grams (g) of kale.
• There is 10 mg of ascorbic acid per every 100 g of apricot.
• Humans cannot make ascorbic acid in their bodies, so they must get it from foods, including fruits and vegetables.
• Ascorbic acid is also known as vitamin C.

The student wants to refute a claim that apricots are a better source of vitamin C than kale is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Kale contains vitamin C (also known as ascorbic acid); in fact, there is 120 mg of vitamin C in every 100 g of kale.
Kale contains ascorbic acid (also known as vitamin C), and apricots do too.
Humans cannot make ascorbic acid in their bodies, but they can get it from kale and apricots.
With 120 mg of vitamin C per every 100 g, kale is actually a better source of vitamin C than apricots, which contain only 10 mg per every 100 g.
explanation:
Correct answer
With 120 mg of vitamin C per every 100 g, kale is actually a better source of vitamin C than apricots, which contain only 10 mg per every 100 g.

Why this is correct
The goal is to refute the claim that apricots are a better source of vitamin C than kale.

This choice:
• Directly compares both foods
• Uses precise numerical evidence
• Clearly shows kale has much more vitamin C

It is the strongest rebuttal.

Why the other choices are wrong

Kale contains vitamin C…
• States a fact but does not refute the comparison.

Kale contains ascorbic acid, and apricots do too.
• Emphasizes similarity, not superiority.

Humans cannot make ascorbic acid…
• Irrelevant to which food is the better source.

question:
• Snow hydrologist Julie Koeberle helps maintain automated snow measurement stations.
• They are called SNOTEL sites.
• There are around 90 stations throughout Wyoming.
• One is at Bear Trap Meadow.
• The data collected can help researchers make downstream water supply predictions.

Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to provide an example of a SNOTEL site?
choices: The data collected by SNOTEL sites can help researchers predict downstream water supplies.
The SNOTEL site at Bear Trap Meadow is one of around 90 automated snow measurement stations in Wyoming.
Snow hydrologist Julie Koeberle helps maintain automated snow monitoring stations known as SNOTEL sites.
Located throughout Wyoming, SNOTEL sites monitor snow conditions.
explanation:
Correct answer
The SNOTEL site at Bear Trap Meadow is one of around 90 automated snow measurement stations in Wyoming.

Why this is correct
The question asks for a specific example of a SNOTEL site.

This choice:
• Names a concrete location (Bear Trap Meadow)
• Identifies it explicitly as a SNOTEL site
• Uses multiple facts from the notes accurately

Why the other choices are wrong

The data collected by SNOTEL sites…
• Describes function, not an example.

Snow hydrologist Julie Koeberle helps maintain…
• Describes a person’s role, not a site.

Located throughout Wyoming…
